subject: Follow-up: telemetry & third-party sharing controls (post-demo)
message_1_body:
Hi Elena / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciated the detailed questions. Per our call, I wanted to capture the items you asked us to clarify around telemetry, PII, and third-party sharing so we can close the info gap for your security review. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps.

Recap / clarifications you asked for:
- What telemetry fields does Redwood collect in hosted mode vs Dedicated/Private deployments?
- Do logs or telemetry ever contain customer PII (customer names, emails, full user content)?
- Data retention default and ability to configure (retention windows, deletion APIs).
- How we share telemetry with telemetry vendors, cloud providers, or marketplace flows and whether customers can opt-out.
- List of subprocessors (current) and how we notify customers of changes.
- Evidence: SOC 2 snapshot, subprocessor list, and a field-level telemetry matrix.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Telemetry fields: primarily aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, error classes), anonymized model identifiers, sampling of anonymized request/response hashes for debugging. We do not persist raw customer prompts as part of telemetry in hosted configurations unless you opt into advanced debugging.
- PII: We treat customer-provided PII as sensitive. Telemetry by default excludes direct identifiers. For debugging captures (rare), we hash inputs and strip common email/name tokens.
- Retention: default 90 days for telemetry aggregates; 365 days for operational logs. We can configure shorter windows for Dedicated/Private deployments and support on-demand deletion via API + audit record.
- Third-party sharing: we share aggregated metrics with our telemetry vendor (metrics pipeline) and cloud provider for infra metrics. Marketplace flows may surface anonymized usage metrics to the marketplace provider per marketplace terms — this is opt-out with Enterprise plans.

Attachments I plan to send: field-level telemetry matrix, current subprocessor list, SOC 2 snapshot. Marissa (cc'd) will confirm any technical caveats.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll send the three artifacts (attached).
2) If helpful, Marissa can do a 30-minute walkthrough of the telemetry matrix with your security team to walk through fields and masking rules.
3) Can you confirm the one retention requirement you mentioned on the call (you said 13 months — is that the hard requirement or a preference?)
4) If you need a signed subprocessor addendum / written assurance, let me know and I will loop Legal.

Would 10:00am PT on Thursday work for a walkthrough? I can share a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[d] +1 (415) 555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com

[Attachment placeholders]
- redwood-telemetry-field-matrix.csv
- redwood-current-subprocessors-2026-07.csv
- SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf
message_2_subject: Re: Follow-up: telemetry & third-party sharing controls (post-demo)
message_2_body:
Thanks Dylan — helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side so we can triage internally: 

1) When you say "we do not persist raw customer prompts" — does that apply to all hosted model endpoints or only for the curated models? We need confirmation that raw prompts are never copied to any third-party telemetry store in hosted mode unless explicitly enabled by the customer.

2) For the 'debug captures' you mentioned, can you describe the opt-in workflow and retention for those captures? Specifically: who can enable, are captures stored in a different bucket, and is there an automatic purge?

3) Our compliance team will want a list of subprocessors that may have access to telemetry data (including telemetry pipeline vendors and any managed SIEMs). We will need to see contractual controls (DPA subprocessor clauses) if Redwood sends anything outside your tenant boundary.

4) Retention: we are aiming for 13 months max for operational telemetry; anything beyond that will be a blocker for our legal/compliance review. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to 13 months or less for data used for observability/telemetry?

If you can get the artifacts and a brief note addressing Q1-Q4, we can escalate to Samir and have our security team set a preferred date/time for the walkthrough.

Best,
Elena
Head of Security & Privacy | FinEdge Payments
elena.morales@finedgepayments.com

- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists vendors used for telemetry ingestion, metrics (DatapipelineCo), log storage (CloudLogCorp), and analytics (MetricsAI). Each vendor entry includes data access scope and whether they receive raw or aggregated data.

message_4_subject: Re: Follow-up: telemetry & third-party sharing controls (post-demo)
message_4_body:
Elena — thanks for the quick questions. Short answers inline and a proposed cadence: 

Q1 (raw prompts): applies to all hosted endpoints. Raw prompts are not persisted in the telemetry pipeline by default. If a customer requests deep debugging, captures are created only with explicit customer consent.

Q2 (debug captures): enable via support ticket or console toggle (enterprise). Captures are written to an encrypted, access-controlled bucket separated from the normal telemetry stream. Default retention 72 hours; we can set to 30/90/365 days per contract.

Q3 (subprocessors): attached CSV lists current vendors and the data scopes. We will provide a DPA addendum with subprocessor obligations and will notify you 30 days in advance of material changes.

Q4 (retention): we can commit to 13 months maximum for operational telemetry for your account. We'll add that as a configurable parameter in your Dedicated configuration or as an addendum for hosted.

Next steps (concrete):
- I will send a calendar invite for a 30-minute walkthrough; proposed times: Thu 10:00am PT or Fri 2:00pm PT. Please pick one or propose another.
- Marissa to join the walkthrough for field-level questions and to confirm the DPA path.
- I'll open a HubSpot task and attach the artifacts formally so your procurement team can insert the DPA / retention clause.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
